question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**whose**" is the correct option because it is a possessive pronoun used to indicate **that something belongs to or is associated with the person or people mentioned earlier, in this case, "children."**
 
• "**Which**" is a pronoun used for things, not people.
 
• "**Whom**" is an objective pronoun, used when referring to the object of a verb or preposition, which does not fit the possessive noun that is needed here.
 
• "**Who**" is a subjective pronoun used to refer to a person or people, but here we need the possessive form to indicate the weak learning of the children.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Children, whose__ basic, core learning (reading, math, languages, etc.) was weak to begin with, face a significant risk of regression.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Which (जो)**: used for things, not people.
 
• **Whom (जिसे/जिन्हें)**: objective pronoun used for a person, indicating them as the object of a verb or preposition.
 
• **Who (कौन/जिन्होंने)**: subjective pronoun used to refer to a person.
